title: Strict JSONMode compatibility adapter: validation for partial/rogue token scenarios
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Streaming responses occasionally emit partial or 'rogue' tokens that break constrained decoders enforcing JSONMode contracts. Some models produce harmless-looking tokens (e.g., stray commas, unmatched braces, stray text) mid-stream that cause our strict JSON validator to fail early and trigger fallback flows, increasing latency and reducing quality.

Goal:
Implement a compatibility adapter that validates partial JSON fragments in-flight, tolerates safe transient anomalies, and only escalates to fallback when evidence of irrecoverable contract violation is strong. The adapter should be per-model-configurable (thresholds/tokens), operate with streaming parsers, expose telemetry for false positive/negative rates, and be accompanied by a broad test harness targeting rogue-token patterns across our model catalog.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: decoder gating adapter, streaming partial-parse heuristics, per-model thresholds, unit/integration tests, dashboards, and a small canary rollout.
- Out of scope: full retraining or model edits, UI changes in Console (observability widgets limited to dashboard links), and binary changes to third-party constrained-decoder libraries (we will wrap them).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Adapter deployed behind feature flag for runtime-1.19 that sits between streaming pipeline and constrained-decoder.
2) Tests: deterministic unit tests for 40+ synthetic rogue-token patterns and integration tests across 6 model families.
3) False-positive rate <1.5% on historical production traces for selected beta customers.
4) End-to-end latency regression <= 6% P95 for streaming scenarios with adapter enabled.
5) Observability: dashboard showing rate of gated vs accepted streams, average gating latency, and top 10 token patterns that triggered gating.
test_plan:
- Unit harness: canonical partial-stream examples (truncated objects, dangling commas, mid-string escapes, interleaved toolcall markers).
- Fuzz corpus: generate 2k random partial-token sequences following real chat distribution, run against constrained-decoder shim and baseline; assert graceful recovery or well-defined fallback.
- Cross-model matrix: run above corpus on models: redwood-7B, redwood-13B, open-llama-13B, vicuna-13B, mpt-30B, and a high-noise/experimental 'chatty' model.
- Canary: enable for internal org and 2 small beta customers for 1 week; collect telemetry.
- Backfill: run adapter offline against last 30 days of streaming traces for regression analysis.
implementation_notes:
Design: adapter implements a streaming-state machine with three verdicts: ACCEPT_CONTINUE, HOLD_TOLERATE (buffer until next token(s) to confirm), and FAIL_FAST. Heuristics: bracket balance, comma/object closure likelihood, common token prefixes, and model-specific exception lists.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged in runtime, default off. Gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% for non-critical workloads.
Telemetry: counters for verdicts, histogram for hold durations, sample recordings of buffered fragments (redacted).
Trade-offs: we accept small additional latency for HOLD_TOLERATE cases to reduce unnecessary fallbacks. There is a risk of hiding genuine contract violations; mitigated with conservative thresholds and rapid kill-switch.
